verdict.rationale: Render's own documentation describes ephemeral preview environments of the entire application architecture for every change, with every pull request getting its own running copy of the stack. That lets teammates work in parallel isolated environments, and non-production environments can be blocked from reaching production services. Nothing documents that these environments are unlimited, and nothing independent or hands-on confirms that whole teams use them concurrently. missing for 10: evidence that environment count is unlimited (no documented caps or quotas), details on isolation scope and lifecycle, independent or hands-on corroboration of simultaneous team use.

support.subject: As a developer, I can spin up unlimited isolated environments so my whole team can ship simultaneously

citations.quote: Iterate quickly with ephemeral previews of your entire application architecture for every change.
every pull request gets its own running copy of the application stack.
Prevent non-production environments from accessing production services.
